title: Why enterprise teams outgrow spreadsheets for intake and approvals
description: How governed forms and workflows replace fragile spreadsheet handoffs — with audit trails, roles, and SQL reporting.
body: Spreadsheets start as a convenience and end as an operational liability. Version conflicts, missing approvals, and no reliable audit trail make them a poor system of record for enterprise intake.
A governed form platform captures structured data once, routes it through explicit workflow steps, and keeps every change attributable. Managers get dashboards; auditors get history.
TopSqill combines form building, visual workflows, and SQL on submission data so teams do not need a separate BI project just to answer basic operational questions.
If your process still lives in email attachments and shared drives, start by modeling the intake fields and the approval path — then automate the notifications and record updates.

title: Connecting ITSM and HR workflows on one data model
description: Onboarding, access requests, and asset assignment should share identity and status — not three disconnected tools.
body: Employee onboarding fails when HR, IT, and facilities each run a private checklist. The hire is “done” in one system and invisible in another.
When forms, assets, and workflows share a data model, a single status change can provision access, assign hardware, and trigger acknowledgements in the knowledge base.
TopSqill solution scenarios for ITSM and HR show how cross-references and automations keep those handoffs inside one governed platform.
Start with the moments that create tickets today — access requests, device returns, policy acknowledgements — and encode them as reusable workflows.

title: SQL on form data without waiting on a warehouse project
description: Operational questions should not require a six-month analytics program. Query submissions where they live.
body: Most teams export CSVs because their form tool cannot answer joins and filters. That creates shadow databases and stale decisions.
TopSqill includes a SQL editor over form submissions so operations and analytics stakeholders can explore live data with familiar syntax.
Combine that with role-based access and you get governed self-serve reporting — without copying sensitive records into another store by default.
Use SQL for exception lists, SLA breach hunts, and cross-form reconciliations; use dashboards for the KPIs leadership checks weekly.
